newsitem.title: FRANCE: Toulouse air cargo traffic down 12 pct in Jan-Oct.
newsitem.headline: Toulouse air cargo traffic down 12 pct in Jan-Oct.

text.p: Air cargo traffic handled at Toulouse-Blagnac airport in the first 10 months of 1996 totalled 20,933 tonnes, a drop of 12 percent on the same period last year, provisional figures from the airport authority figures showed.
Despite the double-digit decline for the year so far, last month the airport reported handling 2,329 tonnes, a stable figure compared to October 1995, an airport authority official told Reuters.
This was largely due to a 23 percent increase in the volume of international freight traffic handled at Toulouse, he added.
In September 1996, United Parcel Service, launched a weekday feeder flight between Lyon-Satolas and Toulouse with a two-tonne cargo capacity Beechcraft 1900 chartered from Air Littoral.
DHL Worldwide Express operates a nightly flight between Brussels and Toulouse using a six-tonne capacity Convair aircraft.
It is also served by French express distributor, Jet Services' which operates BAe146 QC (quick change) aircraft on its domestic freight network.
The European consortium, Airbus Industrie, also operates its own freighter flights from Toulouse carrying aircraft parts.
Airfreight is also carried by airlines operating passenger services to and from Toulouse, especially Air France group.
January-September 1996 postal traffic handled at Toulouse rose by four percent over the same period last year to 16,368 tonnes.
French airline, L'Aeropostale, carries overnight mail between its Paris-Charles-de-Gaulle hub and Toulouse using Boeing 737QC aircraft. --Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax +44 171 542 5017
